previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass status post reversal complicated by post-bariatric hypoglycemia requiring gastrostomy tube feeds and recurrent abdominal pain was admitted with three days of sharp epigastric/left-sided pain localized around the G-tube site with associated fullness and intermittent nausea/vomiting, without fever, GI bleeding, or obstructive symptoms. Evaluation showed stable vital signs and reassuring labs, and no evidence of tube-site infection; conservative management was pursued with NPO initially, dextrose-containing IV fluids to prevent hypoglycemia while tube feeds were held, and continuation of acid suppression and mucosal protection (PPI, H2 blocker, sucralfate) with symptom-directed analgesia/antiemetics. As pain improved off tube feeds, dextrose IV was weaned while frequent glucose checks remained stable and asymptomatic; due to poor oral intake on calorie counts, dronabinol (Marinol) was started with marked improvement in appetite, allowing the patient to meet ~90% of caloric needs by mouth. She received dietary counseling for outpatient hypoglycemia management (small frequent low-glycemic meals, protein snacks, glucose monitoring and Dexcom use) and was discharged home ambulatory and hemodynamically stable with stable sugars, continued GI medications, and planned surgical and dietitian follow-up to reassess the gastrostomy tube with a longer-term goal of removal in several months if stability persists.

EXAMINATION:  CT abdomen pelvis with IV and oral contrast.

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with nausea, abdominal pain. S/P RNY bypass
reversal ___.  // r/o abscess, obstruction

TECHNIQUE:  Single phase split bolus contrast: MDCT axial images were acquired
through the abdomen and pelvis following intravenous contrast administration
with split bolus technique.
Oral contrast was administered.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

DOSE:  Acquisition sequence:
   1) Stationary Acquisition 5.5 s, 0.5 cm; CTDIvol = 26.5 mGy (Body) DLP =
13.2 mGy-cm.
   2) Spiral Acquisition 4.9 s, 53.4 cm; CTDIvol = 16.8 mGy (Body) DLP = 895.2
mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 908 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis dated ___.

FINDINGS: 

LOWER CHEST: Bibasilar atelectasis, but no focal consolidations.  No pleural
effusion.  No pericardial effusion.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: The liver demonstrates homogenous attenuation throughout. 
There is no evidence of focal lesions.  There is no evidence of intrahepatic
or extrahepatic biliary dilatation.  The gallbladder is decompressed.

PANCREAS: The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
focal lesions or pancreatic ductal dilatation.  There is no peripancreatic
stranding.

SPLEEN: The spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesions.  There is a punctate calcification within the
spleen superiorly.

ADRENALS: The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY: There is a subcentimeter hypodensity within the lower pole of the
left kidney (series 2, image 33), which is too small to characterize, but
likely represents a cyst.  Otherwise, the kidneys are of normal and symmetric
size with normal nephrogram.  There is no evidence of solid renal lesions or
hydronephrosis.  There is an extrarenal pelvis on the right.  There is no
perinephric abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL: There is a gastro-gastric anastomosis and a jejuno-jejunal
anastomosis, both of which are normal appearing.  There is a percutaneous
G-tube with the balloon appropriately positioned within the stomach.  Small
bowel loops demonstrate normal caliber, wall thickness, and enhancement
throughout.  The colon and rectum are within normal limits.  The appendix is
not visualized.

PELVIS: The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  There is no
free fluid in the pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS: The uterus is of normal size and enhancement. There is no
evidence of adnexal abnormality bilaterally.

LYMPH NODES: There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR: There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm.  No atherosclerotic disease
is noted.

BONES: There is no evidence of worrisome osseous lesions or acute fracture.

SOFT TISSUES: The abdominal and pelvic wall is within normal limits.

IMPRESSION: 

Normal-appearing gastro-gastric and jejuno-jejunal anastomoses without
evidence of obstruction.  G-tube appropriately positioned within the stomach. 
No other abnormalities to explain nausea and abdominal pain.
